turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come on back, Mr. Hale. I'll get your numbers before Dr. Okonkwo steps in.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is one fifty-two over eighty-eight. Heart rate seventy-six. Oxygen sat ninety-seven percent. Respirations sixteen.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Dr. Okonkwo. You're here for what?
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): I asked about chest pain. Yes or no?
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright. Cholesterol bloodwork, and I'll see you in a year. No heart tracing.
[SEG0013] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Wait. He pulls up on our stairs. Says his chest gets tight.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Not pulling up. Just slow.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tightness in the chest, yes or no?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Tight. Like a band.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does it go down the arm?
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): The arm. Any pain there?
[SEG0031] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He gets short of breath. I hear him from the kitchen.
[SEG0033] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Well, actually, he is winded every time. He won't say so.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long has the tightness been there?
[SEG0036] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A month. Since the lake weekend. And the parking garage was a mess today, just saying.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): So somewhere between two weeks and a month. You don't agree, and I won't force it.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any tightness while you sit still?
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): It quits if you rest?
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): You on a blood pressure pill?
[SEG0045] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The bottle says ten milligrams. One each morning. I line them up.
[SEG0046] person_1 (NURSE): Chart from his last visit says lisinopril twenty milligrams daily.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): We can't sort that dose here. Aspirin?
[SEG0053] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He skips a lot of days. My metformin is for my diabetes, that's mine, not his. His sister mailed him biotin for her hair and he never opened it.
[SEG0056] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Penicillin. His face swelled years ago. He always denies it.
[SEG0062] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ten years ago. He retired from the post office last spring.
[SEG0065] person_3 (DOCTOR): Lungs are clear. Heart is regular, no murmur. Chest wall isn't tender.

[SEG0066] person_3 (DOCTOR): This could be angina, though I'm not calling it for sure. Forget the cholesterol-only visit in a year. I almost ordered a stress test, but I won't. ECG today, plus bloods: CBC, a metabolic panel, lipids, and a troponin.

[SEG0067] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back in one week. If the tightness starts while you're resting, or you get sweaty or sick with it, go to the ER. Stay on the lisinopril each morning, take the aspirin every day instead of skipping, and ease off fast walking until we know.

spec.situation: Man or woman 50-70 who comes 'for a check-up' and only slowly admits a tight feeling in the chest when climbing stairs or walking fast; first denies chest pain, later describes the tightness. Takes a BP tablet and aspirin on and off. Doctor orders ECG and bloods.
features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

bad.reason: Diabetes mentioned as family member's own condition, not patient family history; relation wife not stated.
Former smoking and 10 years ago supported; timing reported by family member, not patient.
bad.text: smoking (description=Quit smoking 10 years ago, status=former, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Patient denied chest pain when directly asked; symptoms were described as chest tightness 'like a band' rather than pain.
Doctor explicitly decided against a stress test after considering it ('I almost ordered a stress test, but I won't').
Doctor initially said 'No heart tracing' before new history emerged and plan changed to ECG today.
Initial plan before the chest symptoms were revealed was cholesterol bloodwork and follow-up in a year; this was later отменed/changed by the doctor.
